newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end mixed despite Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end mixed despite Wall Street fall.

text.p: Taiwan share prices defied big donwturns on Wall Street, Tokyo and Hong Kong to close mixed on Friday as investors showed a contrarian spirit, brokers said.
The index rose during most of the session, but late selling sent it down to close 0.52 points or 0.01 percent lower at 6,825.10. Turnover was a modest T$43.1 billion.

"Despite the plunges in major overseas markets, investors still believed the government will adopt bullish attitude toward the market to support the earlier rebound," said Ketty Tu, research manager at Typhone Securities.
"But the slowing turnover also showed that investor confidence is not strong enough to launch a solid rebound," Tu said.
Paper shares rose on international pulp price hikes, with Chung Hwa Pulp up 20 cents to T$24.8.
Chemical and retail shares were also strong.
Electronics rebounded, with D-Link up T$3.5 to T$69 and CIS Technology up T$1.2 to T$40.
But plastics, financials and steels fell. Formosa Plastics fell T$1 to T$69.

Tu said she expected the consolidation to continue next week on worries over further falls in major overseas markets and likely domestic oil price hikes, although many saw a sound long-term outlook for the market.
For Saturday, a 6,770-6,870 range was seen.
